title: Safelist-driven anonymization and query-time derisking for console analytics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Console backend emits high-cardinality identifiers (user emails, deployment names, API keys) into analytics streams. Current scrub/all-or-nothing approaches either remove too much signal (breaking product metrics and troubleshooting) or retain risky identifiers. Goal: implement a safelist-driven anonymization layer upstream of our analytics lake that preserves useful identifiers for approved uses while making the raw stream provably unlinkable for unapproved consumers and enabling auditable, time-bound reversal for legal requests.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Pipeline accepts a configurable safelist of identifier types and contexts (e.g., test accounts, internal service tags). Safelisted values are tokenized with reversible escrow and non-safelisted values are one-way hashed before storage.

A2: Tokenization uses HMAC-based tokens with rotating key epochs; key escrow stored in KMS-backed vault with access audit logs. Key rotation must allow re-identification for records within a 90-day legal window and be unrecoverable after a retention TTL expires.
A3: Query-time derisking: analysts can request denorming only via a gated service that enforces RBAC, logs request metadata, and requires explicit business justification for re-identification.
A4: End-to-end tests that show aggregation queries (DAU/MAU per deployment) produce identical results when run against safelisted-tokenized streams vs. original raw stream for verified safe fields.
A5: Add monitoring and alerts: tokenization failure rate < 0.1% and a daily reconciliation job report for escrowed token counts and key epoch coverage.
A6: Rollout plan validated in staging and can be toggled per-tenant via feature flag.
A7: Documentation: Confluence runbook for legal re-identification requests, key-rotation SOP, and developer docs for adding safelist entries.
A8: Security review and threat model signoff completed prior to production rollout

comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed on HMAC token format and 90-day reversible window. Decided to use per-tenant safelist with default-deny semantics.
2026-03-03: Security asked for threat model covering token replay and key compromise; Security Eng assigned — added T5.
2026-03-05: Data Eng flagged that some aggregations depend on native string behavior; agreed to add test harness to verify parity before and after tokenization.
2026-03-08: PR opened for tokenization lib; code review requested by Jun and Priya. Performance bench shows 6% p50 increase at 1000rps in staging mock — optimizing kernel.
2026-03-10: Decided to gate rollout behind feature flag + per-tenant opt-in for first 2 weeks to monitor impact.
Reviewer feedback (Jun): ensure denorming API requires justification field and ties to a ticket number for auditability. Added to T4.
Reviewer feedback (Security Eng): rotate keys every 7 days and maintain epoch metadata. Must prove zeroization path — added acceptance criteria A2 and task T5.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy tokenization lib behind flag, dry-run mode (no mutation) across staging clusters
Phase 1: enable tokenization for internal tenants only, collect parity metrics for 7 days
Phase 2: enable per-tenant opt-in for 10 early customers, run daily reconciliation and manual audits
Phase 3: full enablement with monitoring and automatic fallback to one-way hash when KMS unavailable
Phase 4: after 30-day validation, retire dry-run flag and complete runbook handoff
